statement.text: Conjecture Let $M,M'$ be abelian groups and let $B \subseteq M$ and $B' \subseteq M'$ satisfy $B=-B$ and $B' = -B'$. If there is a homomorphism from $Cayley(M,B)$ to $Cayley(M',B')$, then every graph with a B-flow has a B'-flow.

title: A homomorphism problem for flows
